analysis: The PR adds the reusable provider release workflow `.github/workflows/release-provider.yml`. Jobs: resolve-env (trusted-master verify-source before credentials), build-provider, qualify-sdk, build-and-release (sign, notarize, staple, final-archive smoke), stage-release (R2), publish-release (coordinator registration, aliases), validate-older-macos. Security-relevant controls seen: post-staple `cmp` of the flat bin/ files against the app binaries; full CodeDirectory hash extraction; aps-environment=production and get-task-allow-absent checks; fan helper signed with a Team-ID-anchored requirement and no APNs entitlements; the publication artifact is downloaded by id and digest; publication concurrency is serialized per environment; dev/staging/prod secrets are gated by environment expressions. Finding: lines ~1170-1174 (and the same pattern in stage-release) run unpinned `pip install awscli` after R2 secrets and `release_key` are exported to GITHUB_ENV, and `publish-release` inherits `contents: write`. This is a supply-chain exposure for A-005 and A-011 (release key controls trusted hash registration). Not examined: scripts/provider-release-publication.py, scripts/provider-release-resume.py and scripts/resolve-provider-release.sh, which carry the actual publish, validate and download-integrity logic. Also not examined: the composite action provider-release-build and the head lines of build-and-release beyond ~569. Notes: the dev and staging lanes sign with the production Developer ID, and the keychain password is the static string "build" on an ephemeral runner. This matches the documented design and is low risk.

findings.detail: The `stage-release` and `publish-release` jobs first run "Resolve env-specific secrets", which appends the R2 access key, R2 secret, endpoint and (in `publish-release`) `release_key` and `coordinator_url` to `$GITHUB_ENV`. Every later step in the job therefore inherits them. The next step, "Install publication tools", runs `pip install awscli` from PyPI. The version is unpinned, there are no hashes, and it is a fresh venv. A compromised or typosquatted awscli dependency, or a malicious sdist build script, could run code that reads the release key, R2 secrets and the job's GITHUB_TOKEN. In `publish-release` the job has no `permissions:` block, so it inherits `contents: write`. With the release key an attacker can register an arbitrary binary or CodeDirectory hash with the coordinator (A-005, A-011). They could also overwrite the staged bundle in R2 before publication, after the signing and notarization checks. Fix: pin awscli and its dependencies by hash, or use a preinstalled or vendored tool. Run the install before secrets are exported to `$GITHUB_ENV`, and pass secrets only through step-level `env:` on the single publish step. Give `publish-release` explicit least-privilege `permissions:` (`contents: read`, `actions: read`).
findings.title: Unpinned `pip install awscli` runs with R2 write credentials and the coordinator release key in the job environment
